minutes.headline: Commission denied a shed at Sunset Lane and continued the skate park and Main Street parking hearings to May 3rd.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard a request for determination on a shed at 380 Sunset Lane, which it gave a positive determination, meaning the shed cannot be built as proposed. It continued two notice-of-intent hearings (Marshall Park skate park and 39 Main Street parking lot) for lack of DEP numbers, approved an amended order of conditions for a screen porch at 137 Flynn Road, and approved removal of three pines at 360 New West Townsend Road with replacement. A certificate of compliance for 12 Alder Way was tabled because original plans cannot be found.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked whether he can lawn-seed his yard under his original order of conditions and cut a half-cut tree previously permitted; told to go ahead.
An abutter on Lake Shirley fully endorsed the Sunset Lane shed project.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission gave a positive determination on a shed at 380 Sunset Lane, meaning it cannot be built as proposed; one member recused as an abutter.
The commission continued the Marshall Park skate park hearing at 100 Chestnut Street to May 3rd.
The commission continued the 39 Main Street parking lot hearing to May 3rd; the applicant is to clarify trees and add a retaining wall detail.
The commission approved an amended order of conditions for 137 Flynn Road and the removal of three trees at 360 New West Townsend Road with native replacement.
A certificate of compliance for 12 Alder Way was tabled two weeks while the administrator searches for the original plans.

why_it_matters: The skate park and the Main Street parking lot and playground relocation are both still unapproved, so neither project can move to construction until the commission closes its hearings.
The 12 Alder Way delay shows that a missing set of original plans can stall a certificate of compliance, which a property owner may need to close out an earlier approval.
watch_next: Conservation Commission meeting on May 3rd: continued hearings for the skate park and 39 Main Street, with updated plans due before it.
Two weeks out: the tabled certificate of compliance for 12 Alder Way, after the administrator's search for plans.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on five of the six votes, including the $955 Timber Rights purchase, and on most attendees. The shed RDA at 380 Sunset Lane differs: ours records an abutter recusal and a "denial" label, while the official minutes record a unanimous positive determination.
